indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B3.2.1.4: Recognise water and air as important natural resources
indicator.objective: Identify things that make water impure

skills.description: Identify things that make water impure
Describe the effect of impure water on health
Suggest ways to keep water clean
Give an example of how water becomes impure in the community

misconceptions: Water is only impure if it is visibly dirty.
Water from a well is always clean.
Chemicals in water are harmless if you cannot see them.
Littering in a river is fine because the water washes it away.

questions.stem: Which of these makes water impure?
hints: It adds dirt to the water.
questions.explanation: Throwing rubbish into water makes it impure (dirty).
questions.misconception: Pupils may think water is always clean.

questions.stem: Ama sees a river with rubbish floating in it. Is the water clean?
questions.explanation: The water is impure (dirty) because of the rubbish.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think flowing water cleans itself immediately.

questions.stem: What can happen if you drink impure water?
questions.explanation: Drinking impure water can make you sick because it may contain harmful germs.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all water is safe to drink.

questions.stem: What should you do with rubbish to keep water clean?
hints: Put rubbish in the right place.
Do not throw it in water.
questions.explanation: Throwing rubbish in a bin keeps it out of water sources and helps keep water clean.

questions.stem: Which of these can make water impure?
questions.explanation: Chemicals from factories can pollute water and make it impure.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not consider invisible chemicals.

questions.stem: Why is it dangerous to drink water from a stream where animals drink and bathe?
options: The water may contain germs from the animals' waste
hints: Their waste can get into the water.
questions.explanation: Animal waste can contaminate the water with germs, making it unsafe for humans to drink.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think natural water is always safe.

questions.stem: Ama wants to keep her well water clean. What should she do?
options: Cover the well and keep animals away
hints: Covering stops dirt from falling in.
questions.explanation: Covering the well and keeping animals away prevents dirt and germs from getting into the water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not know how to protect a well.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a cause of water pollution?
questions.explanation: Filtering is a way to clean water, not pollute it.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse cleaning methods with pollution.

questions.stem: How can farming activities make water impure?
options: Fertilizers and pesticides can wash into rivers
hints: Rain can wash them into water.
questions.explanation: Chemicals like fertilizers and pesticides can be washed by rain into rivers and streams, polluting the water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not link farming to water pollution.

questions.stem: Name one sickness you can get from drinking impure water.
questions.explanation: Drinking impure water can cause diseases like cholera, typhoid, or diarrhoea.
questions.misconception: Pupils may say malaria (which is from mosquitoes).

questions.stem: Name one thing that can make water impure.
hints: Think about what people throw away.
questions.explanation: Rubbish, chemicals, and animal waste can all make water impure.

questions.stem: A factory is dumping waste into a river. What is the effect on the community?
options: The water becomes unsafe for drinking and fish may die
questions.explanation: Dumping industrial waste pollutes the water, making it unsafe for drinking and harming aquatic life.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think rivers can absorb any waste.

questions.stem: Which of these is the BEST way to protect a community's water source?
options: Fencing the area and stopping people from dumping waste there
Allowing animals to graze near the water
Throwing rubbish far from the source
questions.explanation: Fencing and preventing dumping protects the water source from contamination.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not think about protecting the area around the source.

questions.stem: Why is it important to keep water sources clean in the community?
options: To prevent the spread of diseases
To make the water taste better
To help the water flow faster
questions.explanation: Keeping water sources clean prevents germs and diseases from spreading in the community.
questions.misconception: Pupils may focus on appearance rather than health.

questions.stem: Write down two ways you can help keep water clean in your community.

criteria.description: States one method (e.g., not throwing rubbish in rivers, using bins)
States a second method (e.g., preventing animals from entering water sources)

questions.explanation: Ways to keep water clean include proper waste disposal and protecting water sources from animals and chemicals.

questions.stem: Describe one way water in your community can become impure.

criteria.description: Gives a valid example (e.g., flooding carries waste into wells, mining pollutes rivers)
Explains how it makes the water impure

questions.explanation: Flooding can wash dirt and waste into water sources, making them impure.

questions.stem: A community gets its water from a stream upstream, and a new factory opens upstream and dumps waste. What is the most likely consequence?
options: The community's water will become polluted and unsafe
The factory will clean the water
questions.explanation: The factory's waste will flow downstream to the community, making their water polluted and unsafe.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not understand the flow of water.

questions.stem: What is the BEST way to prevent water pollution from household chemicals?
options: Dispose of them safely at designated collection points
hints: Do not put them in water.
questions.explanation: Household chemicals should be disposed of safely at designated collection points to prevent them from entering water sources.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think pouring chemicals down the drain is safe.

questions.stem: Tell your teacher one thing that makes water impure in your area and what can be done about it.

criteria.description: Names a valid cause (e.g., rubbish dumping)
Suggests a valid solution (e.g., using bins)

hints: What can be done to stop it?
questions.explanation: This tests identifying local water pollution issues and solutions.
